question: Who gave the term ‘homo sapiens’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C. Linnaeus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• From the 1730s until the 1750s, **Carl Linnaeus** devised modern zoological taxonomy.
 
• In 1758, he defined the **human species Homo sapiens**, as the genus Homo's solitary member species, separated into various subspecies corresponding to the great races.
 
• "Human being" is the meaning of the Latin noun hom (genitive hominis).
 
• Humans (Homo sapiens) are the most common and widespread primate species, with huge, complex brains and bipedalism.
 
• Advanced tools, culture, and language have all resulted as a result of this. Humans are highly social beings who live in complex social systems made up of a variety of cooperating and competing groupings, ranging from families and kinship networks to political states. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carl Linnaeus**, a Swedish botanist, biologist, taxonomist, and physician, is credited with establishing binomial nomenclature, the contemporary way of naming species. 
 
• **Gregor Mendel** was an Augustinian prelate, botanist, teacher, and Augustinian prelate who was the first to build the mathematical foundations of genetics in what became known as Mendelism.
 
• **Stanley Lloyd Miller** was an American scientist who pioneered the study of the genesis of life by proving that a wide range of essential organic chemicals may be created from inorganic materials using very basic chemical methods.
 
• **Charles Robert Darwin** was an English naturalist, geologist, and biologist best known for his work on evolution.
